originalTitle: Trump administration asks supreme court to intervene over judge’s ban on USPS mail-in voting restrictions – live
summary: Justice department files emergency request seeking to have court lift Judge Indira Talwani’s order temporarily blocking postal service from implementing plan
content: Chuck Schumer said Donald Trump was “[attempting] to destroy the integrity of our elections” by asking the supreme court to lift an order blocking USPS from implementing mail-in voting restrictions. The Senate Democratic leader said in a statement that the court should not “accelerate a case that so poisons our democracy”. Earlier Thursday, the Trump administration asked the court to step in to allow the USPS new system to regulate mail ballots to go into effect. “Americans are fed up with Trump, his failed war, and his rising costs. But instead of facing the voters, Trump is trying to make it harder for them to vote and hold him accountable for his horrific agenda.” In more redistricting news, Maryland’s supreme court has decided that a Democrat-backed congressional redistricting amendment can go before voters in the state in November. The ruling, a major victory for Democrats, comes after two lower courts first blocked it from appearing on ballots. The proposal could allow Democrats to create new congressional districts ahead of the 2028 election if voters approve it. Missouri’s supreme court has ruled that a Donald Trump-backed US House map must go before voters to approve or reject the new districts, preventing it from being used in the upcoming November election. The development was a blow to Republicans who were hoping the new congressional boundaries would help them keep a majority in the House in the midterms. Trump fumed over the ruling, describing it as “horrible, ridiculous, and unConstitutional” and arguing the election process was being “disturbed”. Catherine Hanaway, the state’s Republican attorney general, planned to appeal the decision to the supreme court. She argued it “thrust our state into a full‑fledged constitutional crisis”. Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries praised the ruling, calling it a “resounding victory for the people of the Show-Me State and a clear message to MAGA extremists trying to rig the midterm elections.” “The people are now empowered to decide what the congressional map should look like in November, not Donald Trump and corrupt Republicans,” Jeffries said. Energy, manufacturing, agriculture and transportation groups are appealing to Congress to take action to stop California clean car rules that it argues aim to “[limit] choice in vehicle and other engine purchasing decisions”. Dozens of groups, including the American Petroleum Institute, the US Chamber of Commerce and Agricultural Retailers Association, sent a letter to the leaders of the House and Senate asking for congressional intervention. The missive came one day after a federal judge temporarily blocked the Trump administration from overturning a set of California vehicle pollution standards. “We strongly urge Congress to protect consumer choice by using its Congressional Review Act authority to disapprove these rule makings. Doing so will protect consumers, our economy, and our national security,” the authors wrote. Donald Trump announced an interim replacement for army secretary, Dan Driscoll, who suddenly resigned earlier this week amid reports of tension between him and defense secretary Pete Hegseth. The president said on Thursday that Adam Telle, who currently serves as the assistant secretary of the army office for civil works, will become the acting army secretary. “He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all,” Trump said. Congressman Don Beyer, whose district includes Arlington National Cemetery, described Trump’s arch project as “illegal, gridlock-increasing [and] narcissistic” and criticized the administration for moving ahead with it. The representative pointed to a report from the the National Park Service – which supports the project – that found it would have adverse effects on multiple landmarks. “This project is not even close to being ready for prime time. The Administration has not won the legal battle over the proposal, which is plainly illegal without congressional authorization,” Beyer said in a statement. “The only study they have completed and released, from the National Park Service, confirms my admonition that the arch would be a massive, unnecessary disruption to iconic and historic sites across the region.” Excavation work on Donald Trump’s “Great Triumphal Arch” project in Washington is set to begin in the coming weeks, interior secretary Doug Burgum said on Thursday. The 250ft tall gilded structure will be built in between Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. “This will be one of the Great Pieces of American Architecture, honoring the history and significance of Arlington Cemetery and befitting the most powerful Capital in the World,” Burgum said. But critics say the arch will interfere with historic sightlines and that it has not received congressional authorization. Three veterans and an architectural historian filed a lawsuit over the project. “We believe that construction cannot and should not proceed apace, and we are prepared to inform the court that it needs to, at this juncture, needs to step in,” said Nicolas Sansone, an attorney with Public Citizen Litigation Group, who is representing the plaintiffs. As a federal judge is deciding whether to extend a ban on the USPS’s new mail-in voting restrictions, Donald Trump has asked the US supreme court to step in. The Justice ‌Department filed an emergency request seeking to have the court lift Judge Indira Talwani’s order that temporarily blocks the ⁠postal service from implementing the plan, which includes an online portal that would track millions of mail ballots. The new system to regulate mail ballots, which came about following an executive order by Trump, has drawn fierce criticism. A whistleblower told Congress that the requirements could result in scores of mail ballots never being sent. The Federal Emergency Management Agency appears to be downplaying $168 million in winter storm damage across New York City, Long Island, and Mid-Hudson region. chineseTitle: 特朗普政府要求最高法院干预法官对美国邮政局邮寄投票限制的禁令 - 直播
chineseSummary: 司法部提出紧急请求，寻求法院撤销英迪拉·塔尔瓦尼法官暂时阻止邮政服务实施计划的命令
chineseContent: 查克·舒默表示，唐纳德·特朗普要求最高法院撤销阻止美国邮政局实施邮寄投票限制的命令，“[试图]破坏我们选举的公正性”。这位参议院民主党领袖在一份声明中表示，法院不应该“加速审理一个如此毒害我们民主的案件”。周四早些时候，特朗普政府要求法院介入，允许美国邮政总局监管邮寄选票的新系统生效。 “美国人厌倦了特朗普、他失败的战争以及他不断上升的成本。但特朗普不是面对选民，而是试图让他们更难投票，并让他对他的可怕议程负责。”更多关于选区重新划分的消息，马里兰州最高法院决定，民主党支持的国会重新划分选区修正案可以在 11 月提交给该州选民。这项裁决是民主党的重大胜利，此前两个下级法院首先阻止其出现在选票上。如果选民批准，该提案可能允许民主党在 2028 年大选之前创建新的国会选区。密苏里州最高法院裁定，唐纳德·特朗普支持的美国众议院地图必须在选民批准或拒绝新选区之前提交，以防止其在即将到来的 11 月选举中使用。这一事态发展对共和党人来说是一个打击，他们希望新的国会边界能够帮助他们在中期选举中保持众议院多数席位。特朗普对这一裁决感到愤怒，称其“可怕、荒谬、违宪”，并认为选举进程受到“干扰”。该州共和党总检察长凯瑟琳·哈纳韦 (Catherine Hanaway) 计划向最高法院上诉。她认为这“将我们的国家推入了一场全面的宪法危机”。民主党领袖哈克
